historical_commit_reports.original_commit_body:
feat(coordination): session bus M3 — coordinator-daemon (advisory) + supervisor

session_bus_coordinator.py is the deterministic always-on tier: flock singleton,
tick loop, own heartbeat, epoch fencing. In advisory mode it writes ONLY two
files it owns (advisory.jsonl and its heartbeat), so a running daemon cannot
disturb the M1 manual workflow. authority: assign is refused outright because M4
is not built -- an unbuilt assign path must never be silently approximated by
the advisory one.

bus_supervisor.sh clones hub_supervisor.sh's discipline with heartbeat-mtime
health instead of an HTTP probe (the daemon has no socket, and the heartbeat is
the liveness signal the protocol already defines). SIGTERM first so the daemon
drains at a tick boundary, SIGKILL only on escalation. Userspace only.

Lane sensing is fail-safe: a lane is idle only when every signal agrees, and an
unknown signal counts as busy.

Two bugs caught by the tests and fixed before commit:
- classify_load() returns `state`, not `class`. Reading the wrong key yields
  None, which fail-safes to busy -- correct in direction but permanently wrong,
  so the daemon would never have advised anything.
- the same task was advised to every idle agent in a tick. Harmless while
  advisory; a double-assignment once M4 has authority, and misleading either
  way since the advice reads as a plan.

Verified: kill -9 recovery in 1s with epoch 1->2; zero foreign writes;
eligibility honours priority, lane-busy, ungranted operator_gates and
non-terminal depends_on.

advisory.jsonl and the daemon heartbeat are gitignored -- high-churn runtime
state. M3/M4 evidence will be cited as a summary artifact, never the raw log.

M3 sign-off still needs a working day of would-assign-vs-actual comparison.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(bus): C49 the watchdog could not see the daemon it guards

bus_supervisor.sh identified the coordinator-daemon with
`pgrep -f "session_bus_coordinator\.py run"`. The live daemon runs as
`<venv>/bin/python .../session_bus_coordinator.py --bus-root <path> run`,
so `--bus-root <path>` sits between `.py` and `run` and the pattern matched
nothing. The pattern encoded THIS SUPERVISOR'S OWN launch idiom, not the
daemon's identity, so it could only ever see daemons it had started itself.

Observed 2026-08-12T10:35-10:36Z: pid 3259108 alive, heartbeat FRESH the whole
time, and `unhealthy (heartbeat age 10s, pids '') - restarting` every ~10s,
each relaunch self-exiting on the daemon's flock. Two signals, one working, and
health_ok required BOTH - so the broken one overruled the good one and "cannot
determine" was silently collapsed into "dead".

Identity now comes from the heartbeat's own pid, verified against
/proc/<pid>/cmdline, in THREE states. Widening the regex was rejected: it keeps
the wildcard-kill hazard the file already warns about
(INC-20260731-broad-process-pattern-kills), and stop_wedged KILLS what identity
returns. The heartbeat is scoped by BUS_ROOT like everything else, so a
mis-scoped test can no longer reach production at all - the accident of
2026-07-27 is now structurally impossible rather than avoided by remembering a
fourth env override.

- resolve_daemon() publishes alive|dead|unknown + evidence + a kill-safe pid.
  unknown never kills and never passes; `once` exits a distinct 3 for it.
- stop_wedged signals exactly one identity-confirmed pid, and re-verifies that
  pid every second of the drain so a SIGKILL cannot land on a recycled number.
- start_daemon refuses to spawn while the daemon's singleton flock is held by a
  live process: that relaunch is guaranteed to self-exit, which is the storm of
  2026-08-12 at its source, upstream of any backoff. Bounded further by
  MAX_RESTART_ATTEMPTS, after which it says loudly that the bus is unwatched.
- start_daemon passes --bus-root "$BUS_ROOT": it was WATCHING one bus root and
  LAUNCHING a daemon that wrote to another under any override.
- source_is_newer_than_daemon uses resolve_daemon, so a stranger's start time
  can no longer produce a "stale daemon" verdict.
- lock_holder_pid takes a path and uses `find -lname`: measured 7.5s -> 0.03s
  (tens of thousands of forks on a 2,200-process host), which matters now that
  it gates the relaunch path.

session_bus_coordinator.py `status` was checked for the same flaw and does NOT
have it: daemon_liveness already reads the heartbeat pid and verifies identity
against /proc/<pid>/cmdline. It is the design this change migrates the
supervisor onto, not a second instance of the defect.

Tests: 28 checks over six cases, including the three the fix is for - a live
daemon with `--bus-root` in its argv is SEEN and nothing is spawned; a dead
daemon is relaunched EXACTLY once; a stranger named by the heartbeat is never
signalled. Mutation-tested: four mutants (pattern adjacency, unknown-as-dead,
kill-without-identity, no-storm-bound) are all KILLED, each still running the
full 28 checks so every failure is counted rather than a vanished test. The
suite also gained a pytest entrypoint - it was collected by pytest with all its
assertions buried in main(), so it reported green having executed nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

bus_supervisor: H-4 — replace the mtime stale-source predicate with a deploy marker

THE DEFECT. `newest_source_mtime` took the newest mtime across
`scripts/coordination/*.py` and compared it against the daemon's process start
time. mtime answers "did somebody TOUCH a file", which is not the question, and
five sessions write that directory: an editor save, a subagent scratch write, a
`git checkout` restoring a byte-identical file each move it forward without
changing one byte of what a restarted daemon would execute. Measured 2026-08-12:
14 restarts of a perfectly healthy daemon in 54 minutes. `STALE_SRC_STATE` bounded
it to one restart per DISTINCT mtime, which in a live tree is no bound at all, and
`MAX_RESTART_ATTEMPTS` never engaged because it counts FAILED relaunches and every
one of these SUCCEEDED. The only thing holding the storm back was
`STALE_SRC_SKEW_S=86400` on one running process's environment — which then exited,
leaving the storm armed for the next launch by any path.

THE REPLACEMENT — a committed-tree deploy marker, operator-authorised by name:
  * session_bus_coordinator.py `_source_tree_sha()` captures
    `git rev-parse HEAD:scripts/coordination` ONCE at process start (primed in
    cmd_run before the first heartbeat, cached; NOT per tick — a per-tick capture
    would always agree with HEAD and the check would be vacuous) and publishes it
    as `source_tree` in the heartbeat it already writes.
  * bus_supervisor.sh `daemon_source_is_stale` compares that marker against the
    CURRENT `git rev-parse HEAD:scripts/coordination`. Two independently sourced
    values: what is RUNNING vs what is COMMITTED. It moves once per deploy and
    never for an uncommitted touch.
  * DELETED: `newest_source_mtime`, `STALE_SRC_STATE`, `STALE_SRC_SKEW_S`.
  * UNKNOWN is preserved and extended: unidentifiable daemon, absent/null
    `source_tree` (a pre-H-4 daemon), or an unreadable HEAD tree all return 2 and
    NEVER restart. Restarting on a missing key would restart every old daemon
    forever — the same storm in different clothes.
  * NEW RATE LIMIT on SUCCESSFUL restarts: one per RESTART_MIN_INTERVAL_S (900),
    stamped in logs/bus_supervisor.last_stale_restart; a second stale verdict
    inside the window logs a loud ALARM and does not restart. A restart that does
    not clear the verdict is not fixing it, and looping on it destroys the daemon
    it is meant to protect. The stamp is written at ATTEMPT time, because by then
    stop_wedged has already signalled the daemon.
  * The three-valued liveness (heartbeat age + pid alive + argv marker) is
    untouched, and `resolve_daemon` still gates the predicate, so a recycled pid
    contributes nothing.

ALSO FIXED, found while reading: `check_stale_source` ended with a bare
`start_daemon`, and it is called as a SIMPLE COMMAND from both consumers — so
under `set -e` a failed relaunch would have killed the watchdog outright. Now
`start_daemon || true`; start_daemon logs which failure it was and the next poll
takes the unhealthy branch where the backoff lives.

VERIFIED BY REAL EXECUTION:
  * tests/test_bus_supervisor.py 40/40 — new case (g): a CURRENT daemon is not
    restarted; a daemon publishing NO marker is UNKNOWN and untouched; a stale one
    is restarted EXACTLY once; the second verdict inside the window ALARMS with no
    restart; outside the window a restart is allowed again (it is a window, not a
    mute). The harness now builds a real throwaway git checkout — the predicate
    runs real git, and faking it would test the fake.
  * tmp/mutate_bus_supervisor.py: 7/7 mutants KILLED, each running the full 40
    checks. M5 removes the rate limit (the storm), M6 makes a missing marker read
    as STALE (the fail-open twin), M7 compares HEAD to HEAD (the VACUITY mutation:
    both sides always agree and a stale daemon is never detected). M1-M4 unchanged
    and still killed.
  * tests/test_supervisor_stale_source.sh 13/13, rewritten for the new predicate,
    including "uncommitted edit + touch -> STILL current" (the 14-restarts defect
    stated as an assertion) and a guard that the deleted knobs stay deleted.
  * session_bus.py validate: schema clean, single-writer clean (heartbeat
    validation checks agent/state only; the added key is additive).

RESTART REQUIRED for this to take effect: both the supervisor and the daemon are
currently STOPPED (daemon epoch 67 "stopped cleanly" 21:11:53Z, singleton unheld,
no supervisor pid), so nothing was edited underneath a running process — but the
next launch must come from this tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
